Below is a **step‑by‑step checklist** you can run locally to

1. **Make sure the file is a well‑formed PMTiles archive** (no corruption, correct header, etc.).  
2. **Discover the vector‑layer names (or raster band names) that are inside** so you can write the correct `source-layer` values in your style.  

You can do all of this **without uploading the file** – just on your workstation.

---

## 1️⃣ Install the official PMTiles CLI (the only tool that knows the archive format)

| OS | Quick install |
|----|---------------|
| macOS (brew) | `brew install protomaps/tap/pmtiles` |
| Linux (deb/ rpm) | download the binary from the latest GitHub release: <https://github.com/protomaps/go-pmtiles/releases> and put it in `$PATH` |
| Windows | download the `pmtiles-windows-amd64.exe` and rename it to `pmtiles.exe` |
| Docker (any OS) | `docker run --rm -v "$(pwd)":/data protomaps/go-pmtiles:latest <command>` |

> **Tip:** The CLI is a single static binary – no Node, Java, or Python runtime is required.

---

## 2️⃣ Verify the archive is structurally sound

```bash
pmtiles verify mydata.pmtiles
```

*What you’ll see*

```
✔︎ Header checksum OK
✔︎ Tile index checksum OK
✔︎ Tile data checksum OK
✔︎ No overlapping tile ranges
✔︎ File size matches header
```

If any line is prefixed with **✖︎** the archive is corrupted.  
In that case you’ll need to rebuild the file (e.g. re‑run tippecanoe/Planetiler or run `pmtiles convert` again).

---

## 3️⃣ Inspect the archive header & metadata

```bash
pmtiles show mydata.pmtiles
```

Typical output (trimmed for brevity):

```
Version: 2
Root offset: 123456
Root length: 7890
Tile compression: gzip
Tile type: vector
Bounds: -180.0,-85.0511,180.0,85.0511
Minzoom: 0
Maxzoom: 14
Tile count: 1 234 567
Metadata:
  name = "my‑region‑basemap"
  description = "Vector tiles for the city of Example"
  attribution = "© OpenStreetMap contributors"
  format = "pbf"
```

*What this tells you*

| Field | Why it matters |
|-------|----------------|
| **Bounds** | The geographic extent of the tiles. Useful for checking you didn’t accidentally generate a global file when you only wanted a city. |
| **Minzoom / Maxzoom** | The zoom range that the archive actually contains. MapLibre will automatically use these values when you reference the source with `url:` (not `tiles:`). |
| **Tile type** | `vector`, `raster` or `raster-dem`. Choose the matching `type:` in your style. |
| **Metadata** | Anything you passed with `--metadata` (tippecanoe) or `--metadata` (Planetiler). You can also store a custom JSON string here if you want to embed layer‑list information. |

> **Note:** The `show` command **does not list vector layer names** – those are stored inside the individual tiles, not in the header.

---

## 4️⃣ List the *vector* layer names that are inside the archive  

There are three practical ways, all of which work locally:

### 4‑a. Use the CLI’s `tile` sub‑command + a tiny Node script

1. **Fetch a single tile** (the root tile at zoom 0 is guaranteed to exist if `minzoom = 0`).  
   ```bash
   pmtiles tile mydata.pmtiles 0/0/0 > tile0.pbf
   ```

2. **Decode the PBF** with the official `@mapbox/vector-tile` package (or `pbf` + `@mapbox/vector-tile`).  
   ```bash
   # Install once (Node ≥ 18)
   npm install @mapbox/vector-tile pbf
   ```

   ```js
   // list-layers.js
   const fs = require('fs');
   const { VectorTile } = require('@mapbox/vector-tile');
   const { Protobuf } = require('pbf');

   const data = fs.readFileSync('tile0.pbf');
   const tile = new VectorTile(new Protobuf(data));

   const layerNames = Object.keys(tile.layers);
   console.log('Layers in the archive:', layerNames);
   ```

   Run it:

   ```bash
   node list-layers.js
   # → Layers in the archive: [ 'water', 'landuse', 'roads', 'buildings', 'places' ]
   ```

   **Why zoom 0?**  
   The root tile usually contains *all* layers (even if they are empty). If your source has `minzoom > 0`, fetch the first available tile, e.g. `pmtiles tile mydata.pmtiles 5/0/0`.

### 4‑b. Use the **PMTiles JavaScript library** in a tiny script (no Node install needed)

```bash
# Grab the library (works in any modern browser or Node)
npm install pmtiles
```

```js
// list-layers-pmtiles.js
import { PMTiles } from 'pmtiles';
import { VectorTile } from '@mapbox/vector-tile';
import { Protobuf } from 'pbf';
import fs from 'fs';

async function listLayers(path) {
  const source = await PMTiles.fromFile(path);          // reads the file locally
  const header = await source.getHeader();              // minzoom, maxzoom, etc.
  const z = header.minzoom;                             // first zoom that exists
  const x = 0, y = 0;                                   // top‑left tile at that zoom
  const tile = await source.getTile(z, x, y);
  if (!tile) throw new Error('No tile at the first zoom level');

  const vt = new VectorTile(new Protobuf(tile.data));
  console.log('Layers:', Object.keys(vt.layers));
}

listLayers('mydata.pmtiles').catch(console.error);
```

Run with Node ≥ 18 (module mode):

```bash
node --experimental-modules list-layers-pmtiles.js
```

### 4‑c. Quick “in‑browser” check (no code, just MapLibre)

If you already have a dev page that loads MapLibre, you can inspect the source after the map has loaded:

```js
map.on('styledata', () => {
  const src = map.getSource('my-pmtiles-source'); // name you gave in the style
  console.log('Vector layers reported by MapLibre:', src.vectorLayers);
});
```

`src.vectorLayers` is an array of objects `{id, minzoom, maxzoom, source}` that MapLibre read from the PMTiles header *and* from the first tile it fetched. This is the fastest way to verify that the layer names you plan to use (`source-layer: "roads"` etc.) actually exist.

> **Caveat:** If the source’s `minzoom` is > 0, make sure the map’s initial zoom is at least that value, otherwise MapLibre won’t request any tile and `vectorLayers` will be empty.

---

## 5️⃣ (Optional) Extract a tiny preview file for quick visual testing

If the archive is huge (hundreds of MB) and you just want a quick sanity‑check, you can carve out a small bounding‑box with the CLI:

```bash
pmtiles extract \
  --bbox=-0.15,51.5,-0.10,51.55 \   # lon/lat box (e.g. a few city blocks)
  --minzoom=12 --maxzoom=14 \
  mydata.pmtiles preview.pmtiles
```

Now run the same `show`, `verify`, and `list‑layers` steps on `preview.pmtiles`. It’s tiny (often < 1 MB) and can be opened in a browser instantly.

---

## 6️⃣ Summary checklist (run in this order)

| Step | Command | Expected result |
|------|---------|-----------------|
| **6.1** | `pmtiles verify mydata.pmtiles` | All ✔︎ lines – no corruption |
| **6.2** | `pmtiles show mydata.pmtiles` | Header shows correct bounds, min/max zoom, tile type, and any custom metadata |
| **6.3** | `pmtiles tile mydata.pmtiles 0/0/0 > tile0.pbf` | Binary file written (size > 0) |
| **6.4** | `node list-layers.js` (or the JS snippet) | Console prints an array of layer names, e.g. `["water","landuse","roads","buildings","places"]` |
| **6.5** *(optional)* | `pmtiles extract …` | Small preview file for rapid UI testing |
| **6.6** *(optional)* | Load the source in a dev MapLibre map and `console.log(src.vectorLayers)` | Same layer list, plus min/max zoom per layer (useful for style authoring) |

If **any** of the above steps fails, you know exactly where to go back:

* **Verify fails** → rebuild the archive (maybe the conversion step was interrupted).  
* **Show shows wrong bounds / zoom** → you probably used the wrong `--bbox` or `--zoom` flags when generating.  
* **Layer list is missing or unexpected** → the source data didn’t contain those features, or you filtered them out with tippecanoe’s `--layer` / `--exclude` options.

---

## 7️⃣ Upload‑ready checklist

Before you push the file to S3 / R2 / GitHub Pages:

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | `pmtiles verify` passed |
| ✅ | `pmtiles show` reports the correct **bounds**, **minzoom**, **maxzoom**, and **type** (`vector`/`raster`/`raster-dem`) |
| ✅ | You have a **list of layer names** that matches the layers you will reference in your style (`source-layer` values) |
| ✅ | The file is **publicly readable** (or you have signed URLs) and the host returns `Accept‑Ranges: bytes` and `Access‑Control-Allow-Origin: *` (or your domain) |
| ✅ | You have set a long `Cache‑Control` header (e.g. `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`) because the file will never change after upload |
| ✅ | If you are using **raster‑dem**, you have added `"encoding": "terrarium"` (or `"mapbox"`) in the source definition and a `terrain` entry in the style |

Once those are all green, you can safely upload the `.pmtiles` file and reference it in your MapLibre style with:

```json
{
  "type": "vector",
  "url": "pmtiles://https://my-bucket.s3.amazonaws.com/mydata.pmtiles"
}
```

*(or `type: "raster"` / `"raster-dem"` as appropriate).*

---

## 8️⃣ Quick “one‑liner” cheat sheet

```bash
# 1️⃣ Verify
pmtiles verify mydata.pmtiles

# 2️⃣ Header & metadata
pmtiles show mydata.pmtiles

# 3️⃣ Get a tile and list layers (Node)
pmtiles tile mydata.pmtiles 0/0/0 > tile0.pbf
node -e "const fs=require('fs'),{VectorTile}=require('@mapbox/vector-tile'),{Protobuf}=require('pbf');
 const t=new VectorTile(new Protobuf(fs.readFileSync('tile0.pbf')));
 console.log('Layers →',Object.keys(t.layers));"
```

Copy‑paste the three lines into a terminal and you’ll have a full validation + layer inventory in under a minute.

---

### 🎉 You’re ready!

You now know exactly **how to validate** a PMTiles archive, **how to discover its layer names**, and **what to check before you upload** it to a static host. When you later add the source to a MapLibre GL JS map, the `pmtiles` protocol will automatically read the header you just inspected, so the map will work exactly as you expect. Happy tiling!

MapLibre therefore assumes the default max‑zoom of **22** (or whatever you set manually). When you pan/zoom past the highest zoom that actually exists in the file, the client asks the PM‑Tiles archive for tiles that are not there → the protocol returns an empty tile → you see a blank map. When you zoom past the archive’s max‑zoom, the protocol returns an empty vector tile (or a transparent raster tile). The client does not throw an error; it just draws nothing, which looks like “blank tiles”. --- ## How to fix it ### 1. Use the `url:` property (recommended) ```json { "type": "vector", "url": "pmtiles://https://example.com/data.pmtiles" } ``` *MapLibre will:* * fetch the TileJSON once, * learn the real `minzoom`/`maxzoom`, * over‑zoom gracefully when you go beyond `maxzoom`, * respect the archive’s bounds/center. ### 2.
